ab_heart_creek.blurb: Heart Creek sits east of Canmore in Alberta's Bow Valley, with most of its walls strung out beside the creek, ten to twenty minutes of easy walking from the trail. Nearly everything is bolted sport climbing, plus a few ice routes. The grades centre on 5.10, with a fair number of 5.9s and a solid run of 5.11 to 5.13, and only a handful of easier lines. It is mainly a summer area, climbable once the snow melts off the lower slopes, and weekends can be busy. First Rock, The Bayon, Jupiter Rock and Upper Blackheart Amphitheater carry the most routes. Sixth Bridge, near the back, faces southeast and picks up good sun during the day.

ca_atlantis_3.blurb: Atlantis is one of the bouldering zones at the Tramway, in California's San Jacinto Mountains. It splits into Central, Upper, Western/Outer and Eastern sections, and it is the most condensed of the Tramway's bouldering areas: the farthest problem in the western section is only about a five-minute walk from the eastern side. Upper Atlantis is the least condensed part, made up entirely of lowball problems with many low starts. The stone ranges from gritty and grainy to cleanly cut overhanging arêtes, with slabs, crimp lines and slopers all on offer. It is all bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V6 and a handful up to V9. Shade varies by boulder and by season, and in fall and winter most of the area stays shaded.

co_indian_peaks.blurb: The Indian Peaks lie along the Continental Divide in north-central Colorado, near Boulder, in the Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests. Glaciers carved the high country into cirque basins, tundra and dozens of lakes, with elevations from about 8,400 to over 13,000 feet, and most of the bedrock is old gneiss. Climbing here is mostly alpine and mountaineering routes on the peaks, from scrambles up to trad around 5.10, along with some ice and mixed lines. Bouldering makes up roughly a third of the climbs, concentrated at Swissco, with grades from V0 to V12. Apache Peak is mainly known for snow and mixed climbing, and Lone Eagle Peak also holds climbs. Weather can turn quickly, with sudden thunderstorms.

co_ute_valley_park.blurb: Ute Valley Park is a city park in Colorado Springs, sitting between Blodgett Peak Open Space to the north and Garden of the Gods to the south, at roughly 6,500 feet. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering on sandstone, with trails linking the separate boulder areas and approaches that are easy to moderate. It is a small park that suits a short session close to town. Problems start easy, with plenty of V0 to V3, and thin out toward V7, with only a few harder ones above that. The South Side Area has the most problems, followed by V-Naughts and the North Side.

on_the_nooks_boulders.blurb: The Nooks is a bouldering area in northern Ontario, north of Lake Huron, and it feels remote: there is no cell coverage nearby. Nearly all the problems are at Gold Mine, the main area, with a smaller zone called Bush Nookies Talus beside it. The boulders sit close together in large fields, standing roughly 10 to 30 feet high, and most have good landings. Every climb here is a boulder problem, with grades from V0 to V9 and most falling between V2 and V5, so intermediate climbers have plenty to work on alongside a few hard lines at the top.
